name: Dredge Mining Collective ThermoVault GX-3 Geothermal Tap System
product_name: Dredge Mining Collective ThermoVault GX-3 Geothermal Tap System
description:
The ThermoVault GX-3 is a deep geothermal energy extraction system designed for urban subsurface installation in Meridian 88's geological context — specifically optimized for the thermal gradient profiles found beneath the Great Lakes basin's post-industrial substrate. A GX-3 installation consists of a primary bore column extending 2.4 to 3.8 kilometers below street level, lined with Dredge Mining's proprietary ceramic-tungsten heat exchanger tubing. A working fluid — a pressurized supercritical CO2 mixture — circulates down the bore, absorbs geothermal heat, and returns to a surface-level turbine plant where the thermal differential drives generation. A single GX-3 tap produces between 4 and 9 megawatts of continuous baseload power, independent of weather, time of day, or grid conditions.

The GX-3's engineering distinction is its Adaptive Bore Optimization system, a Cinderblock AI-managed suite of subsurface sensors and micro-adjusters that continuously monitors rock thermal conductivity, fluid pressure, and bore wall integrity, dynamically adjusting fluid circulation rates and extraction depth to maximize output while preventing bore collapse or thermal depletion of the local rock column. Dredge Mining's metallurgical expertise in deep-bore operations gives the GX-3 a bore lifespan rated at 40+ years, significantly outlasting competing systems. The surface turbine plant is compact — approximately the footprint of a two-story warehouse — and can be integrated into existing industrial structures.

GX-3 installations are concentrated in Meridian 88's industrial and port districts, where Dredge Mining holds subsurface extraction rights negotiated under legacy mining ordinances that predate the current corporate sovereignty framework. This legal quirk has made GX-3 taps one of the few significant energy sources in the city not formally controlled by Ouroboros Energy, and the installations have become focal points of energy independence movements and corporate territorial disputes. Approximately 23 GX-3 systems are currently active in Meridian 88, collectively supplying around 8% of the city's total baseload power.
base_technologies: deep bore drilling and lining technology
enables: long-duration stable power for high-demand facilities
social_impact: The ThermoVault GX-3 installations have become unexpected anchors of community and political identity in Meridian 88's industrial districts — the blocks and collectives fortunate enough to sit within reach of a GX-3 tap enjoy a degree of energy independence that insulates them from Ouroboros pricing manipulation and grid shutdowns used as political leverage elsewhere in the city. Dredge Mining, not typically regarded as a benevolent actor, has found itself in the unusual position of being celebrated as a counterweight to Ouroboros dominance, though the Collective extracts its own forms of value from the arrangement through labor contracts, subsurface access agreements, and favorable recycling ordinances. Ouroboros Energy has lobbied aggressively to have legacy subsurface extraction rights reclassified under the Energy Sovereignty Ordinance, so far unsuccessfully.
story_hooks: Ouroboros Energy has hired a team to sabotage a GX-3 bore lining in a way that will look like geological failure — the collapse would take out the power supply for a district that has been organizing against a corporate rezoning

A new GX-3 bore punched through an unexpected subsurface void and the Cinderblock AI bore management system has gone silent — Dredge Mining wants to know what the bore hit before they send anyone down

A Tier 4 community has discovered that a GX-3 tap beneath their block is registered under a shell company that is being quietly acquired by a Tessera subsidiary — when the acquisition completes, Ouroboros will finally have legal authority to shut the tap down

The subsurface sensor array on an aging GX-3 installation has been quietly repurposed to map underground tunnel networks across three districts — someone has been building infrastructure beneath Meridian 88 that appears on no official record
